summary.intent: Work through the local NEXT-WORK plan for the Callisto release tool (cleanup, test debt, SYS-RETRY, SYS-NAPI, derive.rs refactor), then harden the code and make the CLI fast by benchmarking, batching git calls and profiling.
summary.outcome: Opened many PRs: #202 SYS-RETRY fix, #203 mixed-routing test, #204 docs refresh, #205/#206/#208 init and napi stack (#207), R3 derive split, #325 and #326 hardening, #327 benchmark, #328 bulk reads and the single-pass history PR. Git processes at 500 packages fell from about 500 to 10, and `status` went from 11.7 s to 206 ms. Profiling of the non-git time was just started.

repo: Tracking and handoff plans such as NEXT-WORK.md must stay local (`.claude/plans/`, excluded via `.git/info/exclude`) and never go into a commit or PR. The user objected strongly when it was put in PR #201.

`just ci` runs in per-lane worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`, one at a time. The task-notification 'exit code 0' only reports the wrapper script, so the real verdict must be read from the log's own `exit=` line. Several runs showed 100 or 101 behind a notification of 0.
A stray `crates/.claude` directory created by the harness breaks the workspace glob and CI snapshot tests. Remove it before running CI.
AGENTS.md rules: no session link in commits or PRs, and reversing an ADR (such as ADR 5, system git only) needs a new owner-accepted ADR.

ADR 5 dropped gix for dual-semantics risk (gix ignored TagSignPolicy), 106 extra crates and the CLI needing the git binary anyway. It was not dropped for auth or performance. ADR 6 dropped WASM because gix object reads panic under WASI mmap.
Release harness fakes (gh, cargo, registry) can hide bugs, so black-box tests should use the real tool where possible. The harness cannot make a registry fail once and then recover.
ADR 3 forbids persisted release-execution state but not a read cache keyed by git object id.
The benchmark fixture first tagged every package on one commit, which hid the per-package `git log` cost. Tags spread over history exposed `status` at 500 packages taking 11.7 s.

code.finding: Tag-based selection treated a tag on HEAD as released, which was the SYS-RETRY defect. The fix observes all operations for packages tagged at HEAD. The private `cat-file --batch` reader here was moved to `git_batch`.
R3 split the large derive function into stage functions after pinning behavior with insta snapshots. The snapshots passed unchanged, and a mutation test confirmed they catch regressions.
A git failure during change inference is downgraded to a warning under a borrowed diagnostic code, so the package is silently not bumped.
A 50 ms sleep after the first poll puts a 50 ms floor on every subprocess, including a 3 ms git call.
`changed_since_last_tag` now uses one `git log --name-only` pass bucketed by package path, replacing one `git log` per tag. A unit test checks equivalence across a merge and a side-branch tag.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first. For tests that pass on the first try, use mutation checks to prove they can fail.
When the sandbox blocks heredocs or inline scripts, write the script to a temp file with the Write tool and run that.
Check CI by the log's `exit=` line, not the background-task notification.
Use native stacked PRs (`gh stack`) for same-file lanes and separate worktrees for disjoint lanes.
Measure before choosing libraries: the benchmark overturned the first estimates, and the user's gix, allocator and parallel-parse ideas are gated on a profile.
macOS bash lacks `mapfile` and BSD sed rejects some one-liners, so generated workflow shell should use portable loops.

friction: The plan file existed only on PR #201's branch and was then wrongly put in a PR; the user was frustrated, so the PR was closed and the file moved local.

The sandbox rejected inline `env`, heredocs and scripts mentioning `git`, and the harness allows edits only inside the current worktree, so scripts went through temp files and worktrees had to be switched.
Background tasks could not edit the shared checkout, so the PR status could not be recorded in NEXT-WORK.md.
Several CI runs failed (exit 100/101) behind 'exit 0' notifications, and one failure was a lint error hidden by output ordering.
Three existing tests assumed a tag on HEAD means released, which is the defect SYS-RETRY fixes, and had to be rewritten.
The first benchmark fixture gave misleadingly good numbers and had to be redone with realistic tag spread.
The architecture audit agent kept returning interim results while waiting on its own background work.
open_items: W0 branch cleanup is not done: `docs/next-work-plan`, `docs/spec-rewrite` and `fix/native-resolution` on the remote, plus about 35 mostly squash-merged local branches, need a per-branch decision from the user.
#204 still lists SYS-RETRY/T08-RETRY and needs a follow-up edit once #202 merges.
#202 got an independent review and some findings were fixed. Real `gh`, `cargo` and registry reads are unproven against real tools.

W1 real-service credential check needs a decision on where it runs in CI. SYS-MATURIN and W9 are blocked on D01. W10 needs two decisions (distinct-target graph edges, Python dev group cascade), and W11 needs credentials and an approved run.
#326 does not yet enforce the guard where the executor adopts a version, and its fail-closed registry path is covered by code reading only.

Architecture audit: four findings were verified (silent inference failure, `0.0.0-alpha.1` treated as a snapshot, unredacted git stderr at 7 sites in `version.rs`, the test sleep-scale env var on the production path) but are not yet fixed. The structural pre-1.0 findings need user approval.
Unmerged stack #323/#324: the npm confirmation window restarts after each publish and counts only sleep time, so it can be unbounded. This fix is planned.

Performance next steps: commit-hash manifest batch plus a single tag listing (needs test fakes updated), add a 'time in git' benchmark column, finish the CPU profile on the 4000-package fixture, and weigh the mimalloc musl allocator, rayon manifest parsing, a parallel walk and a check for double TOML parsing.
Gix for reads only is deferred until the profile justifies it and a new ADR is accepted.

Executor performance items remain: serial read-only preflight, the per-operation trust re-check (needs sign-off to move), `release-pr decide` running a full `status()`, and the 50 ms subprocess floor.
The final PR for single-pass history (stacked on #328) was just being committed and opened, so its URL and remote CI status are unconfirmed.
